thread:
incident-bot: Paging oncall — p99 streaming tail latency > 3s for the eu-west-1 streaming gateway. Auto-alert threshold breached (SLO:p99>2500ms). Page severity: high. Metrics: tail_latency.p99=3124ms, active_streams=12k, proxy_queue_len=240. Runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/streaming_tail_latency>

alice: ack — I'm oncall. I'll start triage. Any customer reports?

maria: @alice got a support ticket from AcmeCorp complaining about long pauses in live responses, repro steps and recording attached. They said partial chunks then silence for ~4-8s.

bob: I'm pulling proxy logs now, seeing repeated EPIPE and 'write timeout' around the same window. Sample: ```
2026-03-15T08:12:34Z proxy=gw-12 write_err=EPIPE write_queue=180 conn_id=0x7f3b
2026-03-15T08:12:35Z proxy=gw-12 client_backpressure=true stream_id=0x2a
```

carol: runtime telemetry shows kv-cache miss rate rose ~3x and batching fell back to single-request mode around spike. Could be cache eviction cascade.

oncall-rotation: PD alert routed to rotation group, assigned to alice.

alice: quick checklist — 1) confirm impact surface 2) check proxy threadpool and keepalive 3) try route fallback 4) consider emergency throttle policy. I'll run curl to reproduce.

kevin: repro from my workstation: `curl -N https://eu-west.streaming.redwood.ai/v1/streams/streamid` — I see initial chunk then ~6s silence, then next chunk. Repro consistent.

bob: digging into envoy metrics: upstream_retry_backlog and downstream_write_timeout spiking. `envoy_cluster_upstream_rq_pending_overflow` increments. Looks like downstream (client) backpressure causing proxy write buffers to pile up, hitting our per-connection pacing.

maria: customers impacted: AcmeCorp (high-traffic), BetaMarket (tiered). Both on dedicated routes through eu-west gateway. Support has notified customers and provided workaround (switch to non-streaming poll endpoint).

carol: quick mitigations I can push: increase proxy write window and reduce max_buffered_chunks to shed slow connections faster. Also can enable “stream-fallback: chunked-poll” policy for eu-west route. Want approval to toggle now?

alice: do it. Prioritize non-invasive config toggles first. Notify if we need binary restart.

carol: toggling policies now — setting max_buffered_chunks from 256 -> 64 for route eu-west (will cause aggressive drop for slow clients), enabling stream-fallback to poll. Pushing change — ```kubectl apply -f /ops/k8s/proxy-config/eu-west-stream-fallback.yaml```

incident-bot: Config rollout started at 2026-03-15T08:18:40Z — change id cfg-2026-332. Monitoring for impact.

bob: after config update, proxy_queue_len fell from 240 -> 42 in ~30s. p99 dropped to ~1.8s. Early signs good.

kevin: still seeing a few long freezes for specific client IPs (likely older client libs that don't respect TCP flow). Could be slow consumers.

maria: we've escalated to AcmeCorp support lead, advised to switch to poll endpoint until update completes. They're asking for ETA.

alice: ETA for full mitigation? If p99 stays <2s for 5m and proxies not filling, consider triage resolved and start handoff.

carol: recommend follow-ups: 1) investigate KV-cache eviction pattern (why miss rate spiked) 2) add per-route slow-consumer metrics and alerting 3) long-term: implement adaptive write backpressure thresholds.

bob: open item — root cause uncertain: client backpressure vs proxy memory pressure vs runtime cache cascade. Need deeper trace correlation: link logs to stream ids and timeline. I'll produce a diagnostic bundle and upload.

kevin: diagnostic bundle link: https://artifacts.redwood.internal/diag/7777777777-bundle.tar.gz (contains envoys, proxy metrics, runtime traces for window 08:10-08:25).

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-233 created (streaming-tail-latency). Severity: High. Incident channel: #inc-INC-2026-233.

alice: For now mitigation is in place and customer workaround provided. I'm going to handoff to night oncall in 45m. Will document what to watch. Keeping open until root cause identified.

maria: noted — I've updated AcmeCorp with a temporary mitigation and they'll wait for follow-up.

oncall-rotation: night-oncall (kevin) ack for handoff at 2026-03-15T09:00Z.

kevin: ack — will monitor p99, proxy_queue_len, and slow_consumer_rate. If we see reversion, I'll escalate back to runtime eng.

alice: Action items before handoff (assigned):
- bob: produce correlation traces + upload to incident timeline (ETA 30m)
- carol: run cache eviction analysis and schedule deeper config review (ETA 4h)
- kevin: monitor live metrics, alert if p99 > 2500ms after handoff (oncall rule)
- maria: coordinate postmortem comms with customer success

bob: started trace correlation job — query: `select * from stream_events where ts between 1700000000 and 1700001000 and write_err is not null` — will attach CSV to timeline.

carol: note for follow-up: consider tuning continuous-batching threshold to avoid fallback to single-request under transient cache misses.

alice: Thanks team. Leaving channel open. If anyone sees a repeat, ping @alice and escalate to oncall immediately. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident status changed to mitigated (partial) at 2026-03-15T08:22:05Z — p99 back to 1800ms, active_queue reduced. Pending root cause analysis.

kevin: logging a short postmortem draft in #postmortems and will attach the diag bundle.

maria: adding customer notes and next steps into the incident doc.

alice: handoff complete in 45m unless earlier re-open. Closing live triage session.
